name: Injection
description: User-supplied data is not validated, filtered, or sanitized by the application, allowing SQL, NoSQL, OS command, or LDAP injection. Attackers extract confidential databases or execute arbitrary commands.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements (Object Relational Mappers), validate input against strict allow-lists, limit administrative database permissions.

name: Broken Access Control
description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced. Attackers can exploit these flaws to access unauthorized functionality or data (e.g. Path Traversal ../../etc/passwd, BOLA, IDOR).
mitigation: Enforce record-level ownership checks on the server, disable web server directory listing, use hardened path sanitizers.

name: Identification and Authentication Failures
description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management are critical to protect against authentication-related attacks such as credential stuffing and brute force.
common_patterns: High frequency login attempts from single IP
mitigation: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA), limit or delay repeated failed login attempts, harden session tokens.
